title: Applications in finance: risk, financial performance, fraud and customer lifetime value (CLV)

videos.script: The last five lessons of this course visit industries. Finance, retail, health, a factory and the regulator. {{five}} An analyst who changes industry does not start from nothing. They ask four questions. What does this industry decide over and over? Which indicators serve those decisions? Where does the data come from, and what is odd about it? And which trap is typical? {{four}} This lesson asks them of a lender, Ipê Crédito, a consumer-credit company in São Paulo. {{year}} You build its income statement in your sheet, and see profit grow less than four per cent in a year the book grew twenty-eight. {{vintage}} Then the trap. A growing loan book looks safe, because young loans have not had time to go wrong. Grouping loans by when they were made shows what the headline hides. {{fraud}} Then fraud, where a rule that catches three frauds in four is still wrong in most of its alerts. And last, what a customer is worth over the years they stay.
